data.title: Exploring Life in Pioneer Times
data.description: Students will explore what everyday life was like for pioneer families long ago and match details to different parts of daily life.

priorEra.name: Earlier Days
priorEra.body: Before the pioneer times, most families lived closer to established towns with busy markets. They did not have to travel as far in covered wagons to find open land for farming.

lenses.title: Daily Life
lenses.body: Pioneer families lived in small log cabins with dirt floors and warm fireplaces. They made their own soap, candles, and warm clothes from wool and animal skins.

lenses.title: Technology
lenses.body: There were no electric lights or kitchen stoves in pioneer times. People used heavy iron pots over an open fire to cook stews and bake bread.

lenses.title: School & Work
lenses.body: Children helped their parents milk cows, gather firewood, and tend the garden every single day. When they went to school, all the students of different ages learned together in one small room.

challenges.statement: Children had to wake up early to help milk the farm animals.
challenges.explanation: Chores like milking cows and gathering firewood were important jobs for children.

challenges.statement: Families cooked their meals over an open fireplace using heavy iron pots.
challenges.explanation: Without modern stoves or electricity, pioneers relied on fire for cooking and warmth.

challenges.statement: Log cabins provided cozy shelter with warm fireplaces inside.
challenges.explanation: Building simple log homes was a big part of how pioneers created their new daily life.

challenges.statement: Students of all different ages sat together in a single classroom.
challenges.explanation: One-room schoolhouses were common because pioneer towns were small.

challenges.statement: People crafted their own candles and soap right at home.
challenges.explanation: Pioneers had to make many of their own household items by hand.
